992.2 Porsche 911 Carrera T RS Edition Gets Double Customization Features But Still Looks Stylish
9 photos
Photo: Road Show International / Instagram
The specialty premium automaker Porsche has reached the 992.2 level for its eighth and current generation of the iconic Porsche 911 sports car back in early 2024 for the 2025 model year, and since then it has had enough time to add a variety of old and new versions. But this one isn’t on the menu.
The Porsche 992 series was introduced at the Porsche Experience Center in Los Angeles in November 2018 and quickly expanded to include a tone of variants: Carrera, Carrera 4, Carrera S, and Carrera 4S; Targa 4 and Targa 4S; Carrera GTS, Carrera 4 GTS, Targa 4 GTS; Turbo and Turbo S; GT3 and GT3 Touring; GT3 RS, Sport Classic, 911 Dakar, or the 911 S/T – not to mention a ton of special editions and even some bespoke creations.
The second phase kicked off with the arrival of the 2025 model year and all the Carrera and Carrera GTS models, with the latter getting the T-Hybrid designation to showcase that it’s the first hybrid electric version of the 911 series that went into series production. Later came the GT3, GT3 Touring and GT3 S/C, plus the refreshed Turbo S that also gained hybrid assistance and the most power ever – 701 combined hp.
But this 992.2 Porsche 911 Carrera T RS Edition is a combination of aftermarket goodies – a regular Carrera infused with both Techart and RS Edition features courtesy of the good folks over at Atlanta, Georgia-based Road Show International , who say they now have another treat “for the culture” that has reached the “sold” RS Edition status.
No worries, even if it’s sold, the company can always create a matching specification if you need. This unit is dressed in Vanadium Grey Metallic and features a Black and Blue Pasha interior. It has a purist manual transmission and the 3.0-liter twin-turbo flat-six behind the seats, packing 438 hp and 371 lb-ft of torque, which they say is enough to hit 62 mph in just four seconds while on the way to a top speed of 183 mph.
Aside from the Techart goodies, which include the bump of 50 hp and 40 lb-ft of torque, there are also some RS Edition features, like the color-matched blue brake calipers with gold logos, the complete Blue Pasha package, the blue seatbelt conversion, the color-matched blue OEM fire extinguisher, the complete Paint Protection Film (PPF), plus the nano-ceramic window tint and windshield as well as the dual-tone gloss tag frame and ceramic paint coating protection.
As for the Techart goodies, those include the stunning 21-inch front and 22-inch rear Satin Gold wheel package with performance tires, the catted downpipes with X-pipe and stainless-steel exhaust tips, short-throw shifter and engine on/off delete, plus the encompassing aero package. Cool, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by ROAD SHOW INTERNATIONAL (@roadshowinternational)
